# Abstract

Between the First All-Union Census of December 1926 and the death of Joseph Stalin in March 1953, the urban network of the European and Asian Soviet Union was transformed by Five-Year-Plan industrialisation, wartime devastation and the expansion of the Gulag. Across the 251 towns, republic capitals, industrial centres and forced-labour camp settlements covered in this gazetteer, the combined urban population more than doubled from 16,91M in 1926 to 41,18M in 1953. Rapid industrial construction in the 1930s and factory evacuations during the Second World War multiplied the size of Moscow, Gorky and the coal and steel cities of the Donbas, the Urals, the Kuzbass and Western Siberia, while creating entirely new polar mining and port towns at Vorkuta, Norilsk, Igarka and Magadan.

Over the same quarter-century, war, genocide and forced migration hollowed out the historic cities of the western borderlands and the occupied front zone. Between 1941 and 1945, the Holocaust annihilated the Jewish urban communities of Vilnius, Kaunas, Riga, Minsk, Vitebsk, Lviv, Kyiv and Odesa, siege and combat reduced Leningrad, Stalingrad, Voronezh, Sevastopol and Narva to rubble and post-war population transfers replaced the pre-war inhabitants of Kaliningrad, Vyborg, Klaipeda and Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk.

# Methodology

This gazetteer traces the population of 251 towns, republic capitals, Five-Year-Plan industrial boomtowns and Gulag camp centres across the 45 Stalin-era regions of Estonia (Region 1, 6 towns), Latvia (Region 2, 6 towns), Lithuania (Region 3, 5 towns), Moldova (Region 4, 6 towns), Belarus (Regions 6-7, 18 towns), Ukraine including Crimea (Regions 8-15, 63 towns) and Russia including Kaliningrad Oblast and Karelia (Region 5 and Regions 16-45, 147 towns) at five benchmark dates: 1926, 1933, 1939, 1945 and 1953.

Population figures for 1926 and 1939 come from the All-Union Censuses of 17 December 1926 and 17 January 1939, supplemented for the borderland cities annexed between 1939 and 1945 (Tallinn, Tartu, Narva and Parnu in Region 1; Riga, Liepaja, Daugavpils and Jelgava in Region 2; Vilnius, Kaunas, Klaipeda and Siauliai in Region 3; Chisinau, Balti and Bender in Region 4; Kaliningrad/Konigsberg, Sovetsk/Tilsit and Chernyakhovsk/Insterburg in Region 5; Brest and Grodno in Region 6; Lviv, Ternopil and Lutsk in Region 8; Chernivtsi, Izmail and Uzhhorod in Region 9; Vyborg and Sortavala in Region 16; Kyzyl in Region 39; and Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk/Toyohara in Region 45) by Estonian, Latvian, Lithuanian, Polish, Romanian, Czechoslovak, Finnish, German, Tuvan and Japanese censuses [@tsunkhu1929perepis1926; @polyakov1992perepis1939; @andreev1998demograficheskaya; @parming1972estonia; @zvidrins1992latvia; @balkelis2005vilnius; @kostyashov2009sekretnaya]. Estimates for 1933, 1945 and 1953 are drawn from urban registration books, Evacuation Council and post-liberation municipal counts (1944-1945), NKVD-MVD camp and special-settlement files and statistical yearbooks [@polyakov1991perepis1937; @rudnytskyi2015holodomor; @zemskov2003spetsposelentsy; @khlevniuk2004history; @casu2014moldova]. Benchmarks before a settlement's foundation (such as Kohtla-Jarve, Sillamae, Vorkuta, Inta, Norilsk, Magadan, Susuman or Pevek in 1926) or after its wartime destruction (Khatyn after March 1943) are marked with a hyphen (`-`).

## Regions 23 - 34: Volga-Ural Republics, North Caucasus and the Urals

Table \ref{tab:reg23-34} covers 54 towns across the Volga-Vyatka and Middle Volga republics (Regions 23-25), the liquidated Volga German and Kalmyk ASSRs (Regions 26 and 28), the Lower Volga and North Caucasus (Regions 27 and 29-33) and the Ural industrial region and Bashkir ASSR (Region 34) [@german2000nemtsy; @bugai1995deportatsiya; @tsutsiev2014atlas; @kotkin1995magnetic].

## Regions 35 - 45: Siberia, the Arctic Gulag and the Far East

Table \ref{tab:reg35-45} presents 46 towns and camp settlements across Western Siberia and the Kuzbass (Regions 35-38), the Altai-Sayan republics (Region 39), Eastern Siberia and the Yenisei-Taymyr polar zone (Regions 40-41), Buryatia, Chita and Yakutia (Regions 42-43), the Dalstroy Kolyma-Magadan complex (Region 44) and the Southern Far East (Region 45) [@werth2007cannibal; @shalak2005eastsiberia; @antonov2018churapcha; @applebaum2003gulag].
